newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index posts new yr low, outlook bearish.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index posts new yr low, outlook bearish.

text.p: Bearish sentiment continued to run roughshod over the Bratislava Stock Exchange on Tuesday, pushing the SAX index to another year low, with little change expected in the bourse's fortunes in the near future.

A sharp 100 crown fall in shares of aluminium maker ZSNP helped the SAX lose 1.23 points to close at 167.32, but dealers said the heart of the bourse's problems remains a lack of liquidity and foreign investor interest.

They added that the BSE would probably be hurt even further after the National Property Fund (NPF) announced on Tuesday it had approved the sale of a 15 percent stake in Slovnaft to management-led Slovintegra for 384.61 million crowns.
"The volume (of Slovnaft) sold suggests it was a stake from the basic capital, and in this case the implied price was around 155 crowns per a share," said Bohus Betko of ING Barings.
Slovnaft, the most-capitalised issue and one of few blue chips on the Bratislava Stock Exchange did not trade on Tuesday after closing down 32 crowns at 818 crowns on Monday.

Analysts said the sale was yet another example of the opaque practices that haunt the local capital market, and could be a catalyst for investors to leave a market which has set year lows on a daily basis over the past week.
"This kind of deal will have a damaging effect, not only on the company's share, but also on the entire market," Betko added.
The fund did not give any further details on the sell-off and its officials, as well as Slovnaft representatives, were not available for additional comment.
"This may be the last hit for the stock market," said one Bratislava-based stock broker who did not wish to be named.
"Very few foreign investors, who are the strongest players to move shares here, will trade on a market with such a bad image as (this one has) at the moment," he added.
Steel maker VSZ dominated the floor trading with 201 matched shares and closed up three crowns at 625.

Overall, volume rose to 418,050 shares, from 183,180 shares traded on Monday, but turnover eased to 76.47 million crowns, from 116.15 million. Most of the activity came off market in the form of direct and block trades.
